children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose to a nearly five-year high on Friday, and posted a weekly gain, buoyed by strong rates in its capesize segment.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, added 140 points, or 4%, to reach 3,628, its highest since October 2021. The index was up about 13.9% for the week.
The capesize index (.BACI) was up 385 points, or 6.4%, at 6,427, highest since December 2023. The index gained 20.4% this week.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, rose by $3,493 to $54,791, posting a weekly gain of 22%.
Iron ore futures rose driven by a surge in freight costs and destocking at major ports in top buyer China, posting a second straight weekly gain. .
However, the panamax index (.BPNI) fell 9 points, or 0.4%, to reach 2,448.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell $78 to $22,035.
The supramax index (.BSIS) was up 7 points, or 0.4%, at 1,675.
